summary: The 68-byte Ring0 prefix, PUSHAD accounting, segment normalization and nonreturning aligned C bridge are sound as proposed. Two bounded design corrections are required: make vector/profile dispatch an explicit implementable table, and isolate the destructive null-segment/DF trigger from inherited IRQ delivery so RED proves the intended exception-entry deficiency. No TSS or CPL3 implementation is requested.

findings.title: Error-vector/profile policy remains deferred rather than specified
findings.finding: The design correctly warns against universal no-error classification for 21/29/30 but does not actually specify the stub table or the accepted CPU profile. The inherited helper still asserts every vector except 8/10/11/12/13/14/17 has no error. The inherited QEMU argv has no explicit -cpu. Intel's pinned table defines #CP21 as hardware-error and reserves 22..31; it is not authority for AMD #VC29/#SX30. Merely checking optional configuration before final acceptance leaves the essential assembly normalization choice unresolved before implementation.
findings.required_bounded_correction: Record an explicit table for all 0..31, with mandatory hardware-error vectors 8,10,11,12,13,14,17, and explicit 21/29/30 handling under the accepted CET/SEV-ES/AMD-excluded profile. Distinguish an unreachable/unsupported architectural exception from an actually no-error delivery. State whether #CP21 uses a conservative hardware-error stub despite exclusion, or how unsupported delivery is handled. Pin the guest CPU model/features and a fail-closed observed-profile acceptance check. State that software INT n to an error-code vector does not synthesize a hardware error and is not an admissible hardware-frame oracle. Explicitly replace or supersede the inherited universal helper/comment/tests so two conflicting dispatch contracts cannot remain.
findings.scope: Small design-table/profile correction only; no AMD implementation or TSS work required.

findings.title: The destructive RED trigger is not yet isolated from unchanged IRQ handlers
findings.finding: IDT setup explicitly executes STI. The proposed trigger then sets DS/ES/FS/GS to null and DF=1 without explicitly masking IRQs first, while the design deliberately leaves compiler-ABI IRQ handlers unchanged. A timer or keyboard IRQ in that window can access globals with null DS, or otherwise alter the fault provenance, before the intended UD2. Such a baseline failure is not a demonstrated exception-entry RED and could make the candidate fixture nondeterministic too.
findings.required_bounded_correction: Require the naked destructive trigger to execute CLI before changing any segment, DF, or sentinel register; capture known pre-UD2 state at a pinned symbol after setup and require the observed fault EIP/vector to be UD2/#UD. State saved IF=0 and DF=1 expectations and separately assert live handler DF=0, normalized selectors and correct C stack alignment. Do not weaken the existing ordinary-IRQ regression coverage. Keep host-caused debugger #DB effects distinct from the injected fault.
findings.scope: Fixture/oracle design clarification only; no IRQ redesign.

findings.title: Host harness must exercise shared pure production definitions, not another mirror
findings.finding: The host harness deliberately excludes interrupt.rs and does not expose io::serial; its existing gate encoder is a mirror. Adding frame tests there cannot validate production assembly by itself. A pointer-width-dependent host struct would also fail to represent the i686 frame.
findings.recommendation: Keep the prefix/decoder/profile metadata in a host-importable pure module using only fixed-width u32 fields; keep privileged assembly and serial imports target-gated. Exercise the actual shared definitions, every prefix size/offset, exact-length and short synthetic tails, CS-origin versus PF.user, and negative-profile/vector controls. Check emitted i686 assembly/IDT in candidate acceptance; host tests are not CPU evidence.

findings.title: Existing GDB/QMP helpers need F2-specific assertions
findings.finding: Gdb.registers exposes only ten GPR/EIP/EFLAGS values, not CS/data selectors or CR2. Qmp.hardware parses CR0/CR3/CR4/EIP/EFL and retains raw text but does not decode CR2/segments. Reuse of these helpers alone is not proof of the new frame/segment oracle.
findings.recommendation: In the new owned fixture, add explicit fail-closed decoding or raw-register evidence for CS/SS/DS/ES/FS/GS and CR2; preserve exact 68-byte prefix bytes and argument-pointer identity at the Rust entry. Capture live DF/IF/segments and entry ESP modulo16 independently of saved flags. Verify hardware-error GP/PF raw frames and error values, stable terminal HLT with IF0, exact trigger EIP, no unexpected continuation, and invocation-owned exit/cleanup. Do not modify or reopen F1.

findings.title: Double-fault CS is undefined too; latch is not an emergency stack
findings.finding: The stated ordinary-stack #DF limitation and F3 deferral are correct. The pinned authority marks both saved CS and EIP undefined for #DF, not just EIP. Also a Rust first-entry latch cannot avoid the hardware/stub stack work before reaching that latch.
findings.recommendation: Do not interpret #DF saved CS&3 as reliable origin authority or require its EIP/CS to match a restart oracle. Keep any #DF evidence explicitly conditional on successful delivery and usable stack; do not describe the latch as protecting failed delivery or pre-latch nesting. No F3 implementation is a condition of this F2 review.

approved_design_elements.topic: Mandatory prefix and same-ring optional-tail safety
approved_design_elements.assessment: Seventeen u32 fields give 68 bytes. CPU mandatory EIP/CS/EFLAGS at 56/60/64 are correct after normalized vector/error, PUSHAD and four 32-bit segment slots. Do not manufacture a reference spanning oldESP/SS; production never reads the optional tail. Same-ring pre-exception ESP=prefix+68 is a scalar, not a dereference. Saved CS high16 must be masked for selector semantics.

PUSHAD before EAX scratch preserves all GPRs; its saved ESP is prefix+48, the normalized vector address, not pre-exception ESP. Saving selectors as explicitly zero-extended u32 avoids PUSH-segment upper-bit ambiguity. ESP/EBP-based SS writes allow prefix construction with null data selectors. GDT confirms flat present writable data0x10 and code0x08; no arbitrary selector restore or SS reload belongs on this nonreturning path.

CPU-saved EFLAGS retains original DF while CLD satisfies the Rust/C ABI. Preserve the frame pointer before aligning ESP. AND ESP,-16; SUB ESP,12; PUSH pointer yields pre-CALL ESP mod16=0 and callee entry mod16=12 without overwriting the frame above. extern C ->! plus defensive CLI/HLT is suitable for fatal-only Ring0 entry, not a resumable ABI. The target disables SSE/SSE2/MMX and uses softfloat/abort; no extended-state restoration claim is made.

First-entry atomic latch before diagnostics, CLI, fixed literals/hex and direct bounded COM1 polling avoid inherited formatting/locking hazards. Existing putc has a finite 100000-iteration poll bound. Snapshot CR2 before output and avoid allocator/page-map/VGA/PortAllocator guards or unwinding. Implementation still needs actual call-graph/disassembly review and reentry/nonallocation controls; these are not proven by this design review.

Real DE/UD/GP/PF at both RAM sizes, canonical-body stripping equality, known raw CPU context and terminal nonreturning evidence are appropriate. The F1 fixture demonstrates disposable copying, per-input hashes and complete stripping equality plus owned-process kill/wait. Normal boot and inherited F1 gates must remain intact. No CPL3/TSS/USER/deployment/history work is authorized; baseline identity resolution remains a separate acceptance prerequisite and was not reopened here.
